newsitem.title: IRAQ: Romania to buy up to 150,000 barrels of Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Romania to buy up to 150,000 barrels of Iraqi oil.

text.p: Romanian firms plan to buy 100,000 to 150,000 barrels of Iraqi crude oil as part of Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, Romania's ambassador in Baghdad said in remarks published on Tuesday.

"Romanian firms specialised in oil marketing are to buy 100,000 to 150,000 barrels of Iraqi crude during three months," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya quoted the ambassador, Ion Mielcioiu, as saying.
"The Romanian ambassador said talks were continuing with Iraq in order to sign an oil contract," the paper reported, but gave no further details.
In October, Iraq's National Assembly (parliament) authorised the Oil Ministry to sign a contract worth $26.5 million with Romania.

Iraqi newspapers then said the contract stated that Romanian companies would drill 48 wells throughout Iraq during the next two years in return for supplying Romania with crude oil after the end of U.N. sanctions.

Iraq began limited oil exports two weeks ago under a deal signed with the U.N. on May 20. The deal allows Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. trade sanctions imposed after Iraqi's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
